info.name: Bano Qabil Media API
info.description:
# Media Upload API (Cloudinary)

A **separate** collection for the `/api/media` routes — file upload, replace and delete backed by Cloudinary. Kept apart from the main `bano-qabil-backend` collection so it can be imported on its own.

---

## Requires the shared environment

This collection uses the same `{{base_url}}` and `{{token}}` variables as the main collection. Select the **bano-qabil-local** environment (top-right in Postman) before sending anything here.

No login request lives in this collection — auth is centralized in **bano-qabil-backend → Auth → Login**, whose test script writes `{{token}}` automatically. Run that once, then come back here.

## Base URL

| Environment | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Local | `http://localhost:5000` |

## Authentication

**Every route in this collection requires a valid JWT.** Unlike the product/category image uploads in the main collection, media routes are **not** admin-restricted — any authenticated user (customer or admin) can upload, replace, or delete.

## Storage backend

Files go straight to **Cloudinary** via `multer-storage-cloudinary` — nothing is saved to local disk. Each upload creates a `Media` document in MongoDB:

```json
{ "_id": "...", "url": "https://res.cloudinary.com/...", "publicId": "my_app_uploads/...", "uploadedBy": "<user id>" }
```

| Constraint | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Max file size | **10 MB** |
| Allowed formats | `jpg`, `png`, `jpeg`, `webp`, `mp4` |
| Cloudinary folder | `my_app_uploads` |
| `resource_type` | `auto` (Cloudinary picks image/video/raw) |

## Error contract

Same shape as the rest of the API — `{ "message": "..." }` — produced by the shared `errorHandler`.

| Status | Cause |
| --- | --- |
| `400` | No file attached, disallowed format/extension, or file over 10 MB |
| `401` | Missing/invalid/expired token — every route here needs one |
| `404` | `Media not found` — bad `:id` on update/delete |
| `400` | Malformed `:id` (CastError) |

Cloudinary's own rejection (e.g. `"An unknown file format not allowed"`) is reported with Cloudinary's own `http_code`, which `errorHandler` now reads alongside `statusCode`/`status` — so a bad file type correctly comes back as `400`, not `500`.

## Known quirk — nested path

The collection is mounted at `/api/media` in `server.js`, and the update/delete routes are themselves defined as `/media/:id` — so the real path is `/api/media/media/:id` (as used below). Not a typo in this collection; it matches the current route file.

formdata.description: Required. jpg, png, jpeg, webp, or mp4 — max 10 MB.

request.description:
Uploads a single file to Cloudinary and creates a `Media` record.

`🔒 Authenticated` — any logged-in user, no role restriction. `📎 multipart/form-data`

> Do **not** set `Content-Type` manually — Postman generates the multipart boundary for you.

### Form fields

| Field | Type | Required | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `file` | **file** | ✅ | jpg / png / jpeg / webp / mp4, ≤ 10 MB |

### Responses

**201 Created**
```json
{
  "message": "Upload successful",
  "media": {
    "_id": "66f4...",
    "url": "https://res.cloudinary.com/<cloud_name>/image/upload/v.../my_app_uploads/abc123.png",
    "publicId": "my_app_uploads/abc123",
    "uploadedBy": "66f0...",
    "createdAt": "2026-08-06T..."
  }
}
```

| Status | Cause |
| --- | --- |
| `400` | `No file uploaded` — the `file` field was empty |
| `400` | `An unknown file format not allowed` — extension not in the allowed list |
| `400` | File exceeds 10 MB |
| `401` | No/invalid/expired token |

The created record's `_id` is saved to `{{media_id}}` for the update/delete requests below.

formdata.description: Select multiple files, or add this key again — max 5 total.

request.description:
Uploads up to 5 files in one request, each becoming its own `Media` record.

`🔒 Authenticated` — any logged-in user. `📎 multipart/form-data`

### Form fields

| Field | Type | Required | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `files` | **file** (repeat the key) | ✅ | Up to 5 files, same format/size limits as single upload |

### Responses

**201 Created**
```json
{
  "message": "Upload successful",
  "media": [
    { "_id": "66f4...", "url": "https://res.cloudinary.com/...", "publicId": "my_app_uploads/..." },
    { "_id": "66f5...", "url": "https://res.cloudinary.com/...", "publicId": "my_app_uploads/..." }
  ]
}
```

| Status | Cause |
| --- | --- |
| `400` | `No files uploaded` — `files` field was empty |
| `400` | Any file has a disallowed format, or exceeds 10 MB |
| `401` | No/invalid/expired token |

Each file uploads independently via `Promise.all` — if one fails, the whole request fails and no partial `Media` records are left behind (Mongoose calls reject together).

formdata.description: Required. Replaces the existing file entirely.

request.description:
Replaces a media record's file with a new upload.

`🔒 Authenticated` — any logged-in user, no ownership check (any authenticated user can update any media record by id). `📎 multipart/form-data`

### Path params

| Param | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `id` | Mongo ObjectId of the `Media` document. Defaults to `{{media_id}}`. |

### Form fields

| Field | Type | Required |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `file` | **file** | ✅ |

### What happens

1. Looks up the existing `Media` doc.
2. Deletes the **old** file from Cloudinary (`cloudinary.uploader.destroy`).
3. Uploads the new file, overwrites `url` and `publicId`, saves.

### Responses

**200 OK**
```json
{
  "message": "Media updated successfully",
  "media": { "_id": "66f4...", "url": "https://res.cloudinary.com/...", "publicId": "my_app_uploads/..." }
}
```

| Status | Cause |
| --- | --- |
| `404` | `Media not found` |
| `400` | `No file uploaded`, or the new file fails format/size validation |
| `400` | Malformed `:id` (CastError) |
| `401` | No/invalid/expired token |

Deletes a media record and its Cloudinary asset.

`🔒 Authenticated` — any logged-in user, no ownership check.

### Path params

| Param | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `id` | Mongo ObjectId of the `Media` document. Defaults to `{{media_id}}`. |

### What happens

1. Looks up the `Media` doc — `404` if missing.
2. Deletes the asset from Cloudinary via `publicId`.
3. Deletes the MongoDB record.

### Responses

| Status | Body |
| --- | --- |
| `200` | `{ "message": "Deleted successfully" }` |
| `404` | `{ "message": "Media not found" }` |
| `400` | Malformed `:id` (CastError) |
| `401` | No/invalid/expired token |

Hard delete — no soft-delete flag, and this is irreversible on the Cloudinary side.
